title: Dataset
description: The definition of a valid tcat dataset. Passing this schema in CI is what 'ingestible' means. Fields are required here only when retrofitting them later would destroy information that cannot be recovered -- a deleted failed run, an unrecorded batch grouping, an unstated unit.

schema_version.description: The standard version this dataset was WRITTEN AGAINST, not the newest available. Old versions are retained forever; a dataset never has to be rewritten because the standard moved.

dataset_id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the project. Not content-addressed -- a dataset id survives reprocessing, while artifact ids do not.

batch_id.description: REQUIRED (TRACE-AI B2). Groups data that must never be split across a train/test boundary -- one synthesis batch, one catalyst charge, one beamtime. A validator cannot enforce grouped splits unless this exists, and it cannot be reconstructed after the fact.

lineage_id.description: REQUIRED (TRACE-AI B2). Groups data sharing a provenance chain -- repeated conditions, the same sample measured across modalities, a time series and its own reprocessing. Distinct from batch_id: two batches can share a lineage, and one batch can span lineages.

status_reason.description: Required and non-empty whenever status is not ok. 'Flag, never delete' is only useful if the flag says why.

sample_id.description: The physical catalyst sample this data came from, or a computational-system identifier for measurement_type computational. The join key between kinetics, spectroscopy, and characterization of the same material.

channels.description: One entry per measured or computed channel, keyed by column (csv) or array (zarr) name. Each entry MUST declare units and uncertainty -- see the note in defs/common.schema.json#/$defs/channel on why these are per-channel rather than two parallel top-level maps.

files.description: The bytes, referenced indirectly. At least one manifest entry.

protocol.description: Required for every experimental modality (see the conditional block below). Carries the perturbation waveform and the time base.

embargo_until.description: Optional. When access_status is internal or staged, the date after which release is expected.

provenance.description: Either the provenance record inline, or the artifact id of the record in the store. Both forms are accepted so that a hand-authored raw-layer dataset does not have to invent a tool run.

calibration_ref.description: For a derived dataset: the calibration that produced it. A derived concentration cites BOTH its raw artifact and its calibration artifact -- that pairing is the entire audit story, and it is what lets one calibration id be swapped to re-derive every affected trace.

corrections_applied.description: Transformations already baked into these numbers before the standard ever saw them. Instrument software and lab spreadsheets routinely apply a fragmentation split, a background subtraction, or a linear calibration and then hand over the result under the same name as the raw signal. Unrecorded, that is unrecoverable in both directions: a pipeline re-applies the correction, or an analyst assumes raw counts and never applies it at all. Listing a correction here is not an endorsement of it -- it is the statement of what would have to be undone.

description.description: What was done, specifically enough that someone could reverse it or decide not to.

artifact_ref.description: The calibration or reference artifact that defines the correction, where one exists. Absent means the correction was applied by software whose coefficients are not themselves an artifact here -- worth knowing.

reaction_system.description: The reaction being studied. Free text in 0.2.0; a controlled vocabulary is deliberately deferred until practice shows what the labs actually write.

catalyst_family.description: Material class, coarser than sample_id. Groups samples for cross-material comparison -- correlating a rate constant against a catalyst property is done across variants, which needs a grouping key.

notes.description: Free-text narrative. This is where catalyst pretreatment history, reactor conditioning, deviations from the standard protocol, and the reason a run went wrong belong. The DMSP asks for it explicitly because this context is routinely essential to interpreting a catalysis experiment and routinely absent from structured fields.

project.description: Which project this dataset belongs to. Named in the DMSP's metadata list; matters as soon as a lab runs more than one, and unrecoverable once someone has to guess.

software.description: What a reader should install to interpret this dataset. The DMSP's 'associated GitHub info or software release'. Distinct from provenance.tool, which records what ran.

sample_ref.description: Optional pointer to the sample document in the registry, when sample_id alone is ambiguous across labs. Normally sample_id is enough.

maturity.description: How much weight someone else may put on this record. Absent means `sandbox`, which is true of everything written before the field existed.

stewards.description: Who is answerable for THIS record, replacing the spoke's list rather than merging with it. Absent means the spoke's stewards apply, which is the usual case.

then.description: An experimental measurement without a declared protocol cannot be reproduced or designed against.

provenance.description: A derived dataset must be regenerable, so its provenance record cannot be a bare id with no chain behind it. Enforced by the validator's chain check rather than by JSON Schema alone.

format.description: A raw-layer file may be instrument-native; canonical and derived layers may not.
Canonical and derived layers hold converted data only. Convert at ingestion; never carry an instrument blob forward.
